clue.text: Doctor can predict one will be clumsy

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician foresees that a patient is going to be clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, the person doing the predicting, but here it is a verb telling you to shuffle the thirteen letters of CAN PREDICT ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forever having mishaps through awkwardness is described as prone to accidents.

clue.text: Top theatre's first Evita cast to mesmerise

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of theatre is wanted
to cast something is to throw or mould it afresh, so the letters of Evita are rearranged

explanation.surface: A top theatre's opening night of the musical Evita is set to spellbind its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as the actors in Evita, but it is the instruction to rearrange EVITA into IVATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate someone is to hold their attention completely, which is what mesmerising does.

clue.text: Emu I lift from the bottom entertains hip insider?

indicators.note: from the bottom says the hidden letters are read backwards, upwards in this down entry
the phrase entertains, or holds within it, the letters of the answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nonsense image of an emu being lifted and something entertaining a trendy person on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'entertains hip insider' as the definition, but 'entertains' is the hiding signal: EMU I LIFT holds the letters, read from the bottom up. The definition is just 'hip insider?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilium is the broad upper bone of the pelvis, literally a component inside the hip, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Test disheartened pupil before English lesson

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: the heart, or middle letters, of the word pupil are removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A dispirited schoolchild sits a test before an English class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' seems to describe the pupil's mood but tells you to drop the middle of PUPIL, leaving PL.
explanation.definitionFit: An example can serve as a warning or instruction, as in 'let that be a lesson to you'.

clue.text: Small catch when man working on the house accepts direct debit

indicators.note: the tiler's word takes the other letters in, holding them inside

parts.note: a tiler is a tradesman who works on a house's roof or walls
DD is the usual abbreviation for direct debit, a standing bank payment

explanation.surface: A modest windfall for a builder who agrees to be paid by direct debit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small catch' sounds like a minor drawback in a deal; it is a little fish. A tiddler is British slang for a very small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is a tiny fish, the sort a child nets in a stream, so a small catch.

clue.text: Sensible king swaps sides first, I see

indicators.note: the left and right ends of the king's name trade places, an L for an R and an R for an L

parts.note: Lear is the king of Shakespeare's tragedy
first is written 1st, with the digit read as the letter I
I see, in text-message shorthand, is written I C

explanation.surface: A pragmatic monarch changes allegiance early on, I notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swaps sides' means L (left) and R (right) exchange in LEAR, giving REAL. Then 1ST and I C, as typed in a text message.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic person is practical and grounded, which is what being sensible means.

clue.text: Evening things out, removing wrinkles at last

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
removing says a letter is taken away from the word things
at last picks the final letter of wrinkles

explanation.surface: Smoothing matters over, getting rid of the creases in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening things out' reads as a single phrase about levelling, but 'Evening' is the definition. THINGS loses S (end of 'wrinkles') to give THING, which 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time after evening has fallen, and the two words commonly stand in for each other.

clue.text: Half-heartedly encourage hard nut, struggling during extremely tedious valuable pursuits?

indicators.note: the other pieces fall during, so inside, the two outer letters
extremely picks the two extreme letters, first and last, of tedious
the heart of the synonym is a double letter, and only half of it is kept

parts.note: to reassure someone is to encourage them
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of nut are thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: Feebly egging on a tough nut who is battling through something very boring.
explanation.walkthrough: REASSURE has SS at its heart; 'Half-heartedly' drops one S. 'struggling' turns NUT into UNT, and T...S comes from the ends of 'tedious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure hunts are games of searching for prizes, so pursuits after something valuable; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Material for the Guardian, as per PA?

parts.note: the letters of per PA are those of the word paper put back together in a new order, so they are paper recycled

explanation.surface: A question about what the Guardian is printed on, in Press Association style.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, with RECYCLED as an anagram signal acting on PAPER, and you get PER PA. The Guardian newspaper prints on recycled stock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guardian is printed on newsprint made largely from reused pulp, which is what this material is.

clue.text: Carpet salesman also on edge

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
a rim is an edge
and means also

explanation.surface: A rug seller who also works the fringes of the trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like a floor covering but is the verb: to carpet someone is British slang for giving them a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet an employee is to haul them in and scold them, the same as giving a reprimand.

clue.text: Try to persuade some regular guests

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An attempt to win over a few of the frequent visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue for something is to put a case in the hope of convincing others.

clue.text: Honour a team's first principle

indicators.note: first says the team comes before the honour in the answer

parts.note: a team of eleven players is an XI, as in cricket or football
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A sports side's first priority is honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit (OM) is a British honour in the monarch's personal gift.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a basic truth taken as given, a founding principle.

clue.text: Friend not in the church for pseudoscience

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: not in says the two letters IN are left out of the word

parts.note: the ministry is the body of clergy, the church as a profession

explanation.surface: A friend who avoids church because of a fake science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in the church' seems to describe a friend's absence; it actually means MINISTRY without IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry claims to read character and fate from hand lines, a practice with no scientific basis.

clue.text: Ignorant French article precedes a fight with Europe

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: An oblivious French newspaper piece comes before a conflict with the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French article' suggests a newspaper item but means UN, the French for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware of something means lacking knowledge of it, which is to be ignorant.

clue.text: After reshuffle, Attlee ran for deputy

indicators.note: a cabinet reshuffle moves people into new posts, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: After rearranging his cabinet, Clement Attlee stood for a deputy role.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternate is a substitute who stands in for someone, just as a deputy does.

clue.text: Another hearing actual TARDIS oddly stopping

indicators.note: the picked letters stop up the word, plugging its middle

parts.note: real means actual

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of TARDIS

explanation.surface: A genuine Doctor Who time machine strangely halting.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the time machine in the BBC series Doctor Who; its odd letters give TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a case heard again in court, so a further hearing.

clue.text: Stolen? I'll walk clear of all charges arising

parts.note: to walk is to go on foot

indicators.note: arising means rising up, so in this down answer the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: nett describes a sum after all deductions are taken off

explanation.surface: A suspect insists they will be acquitted and walk free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear of all charges' reads as legal acquittal but means NETT, which 'arising' turns into TTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten gains are obtained dishonestly, so stolen goods fit; the question mark marks theft as one example.

clue.text: Naked celeb acted, discovered by director and chosen

indicators.note: stripped bare of its outer layer, the word celeb keeps only its inside
dis-covered, its covering removed, so acted loses the letters at each end

explanation.surface: A celebrity performed in the nude, was spotted by a film-maker and got cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' looks like 'spotted' in the surface, but read as dis-covered it means the cover, the outer letters, comes off, just like 'Naked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone elected has been picked by vote, so chosen.

clue.text: Drink's rough, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is as it is heard spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a rough version of a document is a draft

explanation.surface: A complaint that a beverage tastes harsh, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech DRAUGHT and DRAFT are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a single swallow of liquid, or beer from the cask, so a drink.

clue.text: Drunk chose to drink lager at first

indicators.note: the word swallows a letter, taking it inside

parts.note: picked means chose

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of lager

explanation.surface: A tipsy person opted to start on lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is informal slang for being intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Houses preferred by sailors

parts.note: pref is a standard abbreviation for preferred
ABs are able seamen, so sailors

explanation.surface: Homes that naval crews favour.
explanation.walkthrough: Prefabs are factory-built houses put up quickly in Britain after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefabs are prefabricated dwellings, so they are houses.

clue.text: Mostly pack rupees after liquidating capital

indicators.note: liquidating breaks something up and makes it fluid, so these letters are melted down and rearranged
mostly keeps most of the word pack, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Bundling up most of one's Indian currency after selling off one's assets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' reads as money, fitting the rupees, but means capital letters. PAC (most of PACK) plus RUPEES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppercase letters are capitals, named from the printer's upper case of type.

clue.text: Phone up after pressure is checked

indicators.note: after places the phone word following the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: up says the word is read from the bottom up in this down entry

parts.note: to dial is to phone

explanation.surface: Calling someone once the strain has been brought under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checked' looks like a verb meaning restrained but is an adjective for a pattern of squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a cloth with a tartan pattern of crossing stripes, so a checked design.

clue.text: Smell carrion meat every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then picks alternate letters, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Rotting flesh gives off a whiff from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is an odour, usually a pleasant one, so a smell.

clue.text: Panic room beneath sadly unfinished

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece beneath another comes after it
unfinished says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow, said sadly

explanation.surface: A sense of dread in a room down below, left sadly incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or dread, the same feeling as panic.

clue.text: Volunteers guarding international artist's jewellery

indicators.note: the volunteers' letters stand guard around the other letter

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers protecting a famous painter's gems.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British army's part-time volunteer reserve; an RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Soldier with drug amongst 11 raving — forging bond

indicators.note: the other pieces go amongst the shuffled letters, inside them
raving means wild and uncontrolled, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 11 across is the word ARGUE
a soldier ant is a worker of the ant colony, so an ant is a soldier
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A soldier on drugs, raving among arguments, is forging a pact.
explanation.walkthrough: A number in a clue stands for that entry's answer. 'raving' rearranges it to GUARE; a soldier ant is the colony's defender, and E is slang for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a formal pledge or surety, which is one meaning of a bond.

clue.text: Meter is broken, coming outside to get plug

indicators.note: the coming word sits outside, wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: advent means a coming or arrival

indicators.note: broken says the letters of the words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A faulty electricity meter needs a new plug fitted around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' suggests an electrical fitting but means a promotional mention. 'broken' rearranges METER IS into RTISEME.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a product is to promote it, so a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement.
